title: Regional price sensitivity & headcount cascade
content:
Executive summary:

This working doc introduces a regionally-weighted pricing sensitivity framework tied to a headcount cascade (hiring phasing that skews by region and role). The goal is to provide leadership with a compact playbook to:
- quantify margin impact from targeted price moves in NA / EMEA / APAC buckets,
- identify hire/hold triggers for Eng/Infra/Support when price or demand deviates, and
- recommend short-term operational levers to preserve unit economics while maintaining SLAs.

This version is a draft model + runbook meant for cross-functional review. Not final numbers — model pulls from Q3 usage telemetry and current people cost bands.

Key principles and constraints:
1) Local elasticity: customer sensitivity differs by region and product (hosted API vs Dedicated). We treat them separately.
2) Hiring cascade: hires are staged in three waves (t0: immediate tactical hires; t1: ramp hires over 3–6 months; t2: strategic hires 6–18 months). Each wave can be regionally biased.
3) Operational levers prioritized by speed-to-execute: (fast) burst capacity reserves and promo credits; (medium) quantization/instance mix changes; (slow) pricing tiers and new commitment plans.

Assumptions (baseline inputs used in model):
- Baseline ARR mix by region: NA 56%, EMEA 30%, APAC 14%
- Token mix by product: Hosted API 65% of tokens, Dedicated 25%, Private 10%
- Blended gross margin today: 48% (pre-SG&A), assumed fixed for infra ops until capacity scaling points
- Average fully-burdened cost per hire (eng/infra/support): NA $240k, EMEA $165k, APAC $120k (annual)
- Mean token bill per customer (monthly active): $3.2k for mid-market, $18k for enterprise
- Model latency/SLA risk threshold: sustained queueing or latency > 95th p95 target for > 48 hours triggers capacity hiring

Base-case projection (simple table placeholder — values are monthly averages derived from Q3 telemetry):

Metric | NA | EMEA | APAC
------ | --- | ---- | ----
Monthly tokens (B) | 420 | 225 | 105
Revenue (k USD) | 4,200 | 2,250 | 840
Blended unit margin | 50% | 46% | 42%
Estimated hires triggered at +20% traffic | 8 FTE | 5 FTE | 3 FTE

Scenario set A — regional price move (short experiment):
- S1 (NA +10% list price, trial credits -20%): expected demand elasticity -6% (conservative), immediate revenue bump +3.4% net after churn in first 3 months.
- S2 (EMEA +8% with localized commit tiers): elasticity -12%, revenue neutral but increases average ticket size; headcount triggers delayed ~2 months.
- S3 (APAC +5% with improved comms): elasticity -3%, revenue +1.5%, little hiring impact.

For each Sx we run 3 internal checks: token churn (30d), top-10 customer revenue delta, infra utilization delta.

Scenario set B — demand shock and headcount cascading:
- Shock B1: sudden +30% tokens in NA for two months due to enterprise pilot. Model result: infra utilization to 92% of reserved capacity -> recommend immediate t0 hires: 3 infra SREs (NA) and convert 2 contractors to FTE. Approve burst pool drawdown to retain latency SLO.
- Shock B2: price compression in enterprise deals (avg discount delta -7%) across EMEA -> revenue down -4% over 90d; recommend hiring pause for t1 engineers, freeze non-critical GtM hires in region, accelerate cost-optimization (quantize models, enable prefix caching).

Sensitivity matrix (high level):
- Price change magnitude vs margin impact: small price increases in NA (<=8%) have muted elasticity; large increases (>12%) cross threshold where churn risk to expansion-heavy customers spikes.
- Headcount multiplier: each additional infra hire in NA reduces expected latency breach probability by ~11% for similar workload (diminishing returns beyond 12 hires).
- Time-to-hire effect: adding 1–2 month recruiting delay raises short-term reliance on burst capacity reserves and increases contractor spend.

Break-even quick checks (rules of thumb):
- For NA hosted API price +7%: incremental gross contribution pays for 1 senior infra hire (fully-burdened) if churn <=8% in the 90d window.
- For EMEA commitment tier introduction: requires 2.5% lift in average ticket to cover platform localization and billing compliance one-time cost.

Operational playbook (if approved price change):
1) Pre-launch (T-14 days): notify top 20 customers in region via account teams; prepare promo credits and rapid rollback path; schedule infra ops standby.
2) Launch (T0–T30): monitor token-level churn, top-customer revenue, p95 latency. Rolling checkpoint every 72 hours.
3) Trigger matrix:
   - If churn >12% or top-5 customer revenue loss >18% => auto rollback + activate discount ladder.
   - If infra p95 latency increases >15% for 24h => draw down burst reserve, queue canary routing to Dedicated pools.
   - If revenue uplift < target and churn low => proceed to t1 hiring (regionally biased).
4) Post 90-day review: decide whether price move is permanent, revert, or adjust commitments.

Headcount cascade template (example for NA hosted surge):
- t0 (0–6 weeks): 3 contractors -> 2 converts, 1 immediate infra SRE hire (on-contract).
- t1 (2–6 months): 4 hires (2 infra, 1 eng runtime, 1 product ops) if utilization holds >85%.
- t2 (6–18 months): strategic hires (model engineering, capacity planning) contingent on sustainable ARR growth >10% q/q.

Financial sensitivity outputs (sample outputs from run):
- NA +10% price: 90d incremental revenue +3.8% -> headcount delta +1 FTE net over 6 months, gross margin +1.2 p.p.
- EMEA commit-tier: neutral revenue first 3 months, ARR quality improves, reduces churn risk for enterprise 9–12 months out.
- APAC micro-increase: negligible hiring impact; consider marketing conversion before pricing.

Decision levers and governance:
- Pricing experimentation must be approved by Pricing Council (Finance + CRO + Product) for any list price move >5% in a region.
- Hiring cascade beyond t0 requires CFO sign-off when projected incremental ARR payback >12 months.
- Runbook ops: SRE on-call + solutions engineering pairing for 30 days post-change.

Data sources and model caveats:
- Inputs: Q3 usage telemetry, contract pipeline from sales, headcount cost bands from HR, cloud infra bills (temporary anonymized).
- Caveats: model assumes homogeneous elasticity inside region buckets which will understate skews inside verticals (L&D vs productized SaaS customers). This draft does not include tax/KP carveouts per locale.

Immediate asks for review (action items):
- Finance: sanity check blended margin assumptions and revise fully-burdened hire costs if HR has updated bands (assigned: Jon Park).
- Sales/Rev Ops: provide a list of top 30 at-risk customers by region for targeted comms (assigned: Lena Ortiz).
- Eng/Infra: confirm burst pool capacity and estimated cost per day at 80–95% utilization (assigned: Marcus Li).

Next steps and timeline:
- Internal review cycle: 1 week (comments due 2026-11-11).
- Run small roll-out experiment in NA for a +5% list trial on a controlled cohort by 2026-11-25 (requires Pricing Council greenlight).
- Build a second-pass model that ex-ante segments elasticity by vertical and ticket-decile (deliverable 2026-12-10).

Appendix (quick checklist for CFO sign-off):
- [ ] Confirm blended margin inputs and confirm long-term run rate assumptions.
- [ ] Approve T-14 customer comms template.
- [ ] Approve $Xk burst reserve budget (placeholder) for 60 days.
- [ ] Agree rollback authority and owner.

Notes to reviewers:
- This doc is intentionally concise to facilitate rapid iteration. Expect follow-ups: a more detailed spreadsheet with scenario toggles (model version v0.2) will be attached to the Confluence page linked above.

End of doc.
